steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Young bard, I cannot give you an answer. Let those who come after give it!

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Now, as it just so happens, I have one more matter of vital importance to relay to you all tonight.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: –I'm afraid this will be the Clan of Tarans' final gathering.

steps.name: Witty Noble
steps.text: Well, now, what are you saying, Your Lordship? Hasn't our cause only just begun?

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Fret not. It is true that the cause of we Tarans to seek who we are is fresh and anew. What will cease to exist is merely the humble little gathering that I lead as an individual.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: —Isn't that right, my dear, loyal servant?

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: *cough*, *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Earl's Attendant
steps.text: My apologies... I'm but a servant. I don't presume to understand.

steps.name: Earl's Attendant
steps.text: It's snowing heavily outside. Your body is frail... I can ready the car for you at any moment.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: No need.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Mr. Williams, would you share a walk with me on this snow-filled day?

steps.name: Plain-Dressed Bard
steps.text: It would be my honor. The inn I'm staying in had no firewood to begin with. There isn't much left for the snow to hinder.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Really? I see... Yes, I never did prevent City Council from imposing winter taxes on the Taran districts.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Everyone deserves at least a warm fire on a chilly day like this.

steps.name: Earl of Warwick
steps.text: Come. Maybe we can chat some more about your creations, the stories you collected in these villages, and what Tara could—should—have been.

a.text: 'May death connect us with all legends.'

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Quiet, did you hear those footsteps? They sound heavy. They'll be pretty tough for soldiers.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Move, move, move, this way! We'll hide in the other direction!

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: The campfire's still burning... I can take a piece of timber as a torch.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Alright, I'll go with you to fetch it in a moment.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Hey! Reed! You hear me?!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Reeeeed—

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: There's no response... Quick, hide over here! We'll split into two groups in a minute, then look for her!

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: And even if we can't find her, we need to find Bagpipe and Ch'en!

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Tch.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: You dare interfere with a military operation?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Something wrong? If I can't shake you, I'll fight you. Not like I haven't scrapped with you Victorian soldiers before.
'Reed.'
Cry after cry cuts through the smoke and mist.
Reed knows the way she should go.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: They shouldn't be dragged into this conflict. I have to help them—

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: —Ungh!

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: Unfortunate. A few inches shy.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Hm? I recall having reported to the Leader about this, but not anyone else...

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: You can't possibly be so naive as to think you're the only one in Dublinn to form your own intelligence network.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: If you're to bring that puppet back, I'm afraid there is no course of action more suitable at present than mobilizing my squadron.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: My, how grateful I am, then... Are you seeking to supervise my work? Or is it more that you'd like to eliminate her yourself?

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: Should she refuse her identity as a shadow, my blade will be faster than your Arts.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: I've seen how diverse viewpoints can be in this masterless Victoria. There is no need for Dublinn to continue staging such a charade.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: If you've come to kill me... does that mean—Dublinn is prepared?

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: You are the only uncertainty left.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: I thought that as a puppet, you would at least learn how to think, at least pretend. I thought you'd have the capacity to set your sights farther. It is disappointing, however, to see your foolish kindness.

spans.text: I thought that as a puppet, you would at least learn how to think,
pretend. I thought you'd have the capacity to set your sights farther. It is disappointing, however, to see your foolish kindness.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: If you had followed the spectre force's code of operation from the start and eliminated all witnesses, things would not have taken one wrong turn after another. The situation we find ourselves in now would never have developed.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: A second wound. Far from enough to stop a Draco in her tracks, but I'm sure you know that even though no other Dublinn militant is bound your way, this remains a one-sided battle.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: I cannot see what right you have to instigate this petty coup d'état against the Leader.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Heeyy—Helloooo—

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: (...The Taran civilians are down this direction. If Bagpipe and Reed hear the shouts, they'll definitely break through this way too.)

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Hang in there! I'm coming!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Ch'en? Thank god, someone finally responded...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: —That was fast! Where did that come from?
Ch'en Hui-chieh. Superintendent Ch'en.
Ch'en thrusts in the direction of the voice, only to find her blade hitting nothing but thick fog.
She feels a chill.
Have you ever considered the troubles you could bring Wei Yenwu by attacking the Victorian army here?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: ...I'm doing this because I want to. What does this have to do with him?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I'm simply rescuing the innocents who were dragged into this conflict. If you're going to criticize my actions from a diplomatic angle, I suggest you reflect on your own first.
You may be attempting to gloss over how complicated these events truly are. That said, I still have a question for you. Take your time to answer, though.
Why did you come to Victoria?
Or perhaps I should ask, who did you come to Victoria for?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: My upbringing, my family, and my personal grudges have nothing to do with the conflict unfolding before us right now.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: At this moment, no matter what you suspect, I will only answer with the blade I hold in my hand.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Now—

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Back off.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Found you, Mr. Fischer!

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: You don't seem to have come for peace talks.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Dublinn's forces are right before us. I'm sure you know who your enemy is here.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Sorry, but my mission's to rescue everyone... You had your forces planted in advance, and you've got Arts protection. There's no breakin' through this for us if we don't get rid of the mist.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: You can try to stop me, then.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Neutralize her. Don't waste any time.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: Understood!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Huff... If only I had some ammo on me. Goin' to be a right pain dealin' with multiple at once.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: 2nd Tempest Platoon member Fiona Young, codename 'Bagpipe.'

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: I've read every single report you submitted on the County Hillock Incident. You have my utmost respect for your actions.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: If at all possible, we should be joining forces, not pointing our weapons at one another.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: And considering you're still investigating the truth behind the County Hillock Incident, we can follow standard procedure and interrogate any and all Dublinn personnel we capture here and give you any information you want.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh, I'll pass. I'm bad at tellin' if someone's lyin' or not, and I'm not the best at interrogation, either.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: As a show of sincerity, I can give you a single piece of information right now.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: The Redsteel Guard.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: You know who they are, don't you? Now—take notice of the combat style of the Dublinn forces here tonight.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, I think visibility improved a bit just now... I reckon keepin' Originium Arts like this goin' got to take a toll, right?

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Not such a toll that it would affect my plan. And I won't allow anyone to get in its way either, of course.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: You could say that this war belongs to we, the intelligence workers... There won't be a single misstep from me. I strive to ensure true war does not break out, and millions continue to live in peace.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: No, see, sure, missions end good or bad, but right or wrong? That's hard to judge.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: A rock...?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, Mr. Fionn! Why'd you come all the way out here on your lonesome? It's dangerous!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I-I don't know. I got lost in the mist. Haha...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Look, I'm not joking, I MEAN dangerous! Hurry up and leave!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* I know... but I have to help. Some of them are in even greater danger...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I-It's fine. I can handle myself. You really don't need to worry about me. I can knock out a man at a time with this hoe here.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: You lot. You're armed with nothing but scavenger pickings. Broken swords and dulled sabers. Who are you to stand in our way?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Hah, you're out to capture our Leader! Who are you to say what we can and can't do?

spans.text: Hah, you're out to capture our Leader! Who are
to say what we can and can't do?

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: Leader? So you really are...

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Working together? That's right. Why else would we come here to rescue her?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: She can fight, and she can guide the way when we leg it. We need her.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: ...Trying a rear ambush?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Nice one, Moran!

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: No luck, I can't pierce the armor with this duff knife...

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Hey—don't use your torch. Your timber's not even oiled. It'll go out easy...

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: Urff—bloody hell!
All she catches sight of is the soldier's burned arm. He swings his military saber, his face a mix of agony and anger.
The saber swipes past her hand, cleaving the torch into two. The lit end falls into the mud, and goes out softly in a puff of smoke.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Hah... okay, not bad. Now he's gonna have trouble with his blade.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Here, I'll hold onto you.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Phew... Hey, how much longer can you hold that, you think? Don't push yourself.

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: Don't make me laugh. So you can resist a little. What else?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: ...Selmon, leave me be.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I hear a few more coming this way. You hear that too, don't you?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: ...I do.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Tarans...?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Us? That's right.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: But I took these rags from someone dead. I'm not with your group...

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Best leave, Tarans. Go somewhere safe.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...I never said—I wanted to make an enemy of her.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I want to correct—the mistakes she made. Nothing more.

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: You seek moralistic perfection in the face of war?

steps.name: 'The Brigadier'
steps.text: Then be the coward and hypocrite you are. Find yourself coerced again like in Hillock, betrayed again like in Peninsula.
The blade tears the night wind asunder. The sharp clang of metal and the interrogative of the officer lunge as one at Reed.
But she doesn't listen. She can hear wails far sharper in the winds.
She knows there are defenseless Tarans shedding blood in this conflict, falling, right this moment.
She could call out the names of each and every one of those wailing. It was but a few hours ago—when she'd heard their voices sing the folksong of home.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...She simply—cannot hear these cries.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Have you ever asked yourself—who the Tarans you're saving are?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Fire...?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: You guys... Watch out for Reed's Originium Arts!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: She's very powerful right now.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: But these flames... don't seem like her own.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: A Draco's flames are beautiful, wouldn't you agree?

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: ...They do not exceed what I anticipated, Harmonie.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Still, we do have a poor soul right here stupefied by the show.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: It's too bad, really. You don't know me yet. Just like you never got to properly know your friend next to you there.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: But thanks are due, I will say, for you putting up such a diligent fight against this Victorian's squad. His Arts are dilute enough not to impact our giving chase now.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: ...It's like County Hillock again. The more valiant you are, the sorrier I feel for you.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: The battle here is over, so you're free to go now. Dublinn won't lay a finger on you... They could even escort you, if you'd like.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: ...I'll pass.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: W-What's she saying? Bagpipe, do you know her? Are we fighting her or not?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: No... Let's go.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: We need to fetch Reed.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: —You're very kind to her.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Of course I would've silenced her. If it wasn't for the Taran next to her.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Still, if she can make our Draco realize she has nowhere to belong but Dublinn, then that's all the better.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Your forces seem to have assembled towards my end now.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Indeed. The poor child's fleeing northwest under our pursuit.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Heh. Much further, and she'll be in the heart of Duke Wellington's domain.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Once she's there, everything she does will be under Dublinn's thumb.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: So the priority right now is... shall we say, dealing with everyone who knows too much.

spans.text: So the priority right now is... shall we say,
with everyone who knows too much.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: In the unlikely event you live to send intel back, it won't be much more than what your death itself would've told them.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Selmon, slow down... I'm having trouble keeping up. Where are we?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Must've run about two hundred meters into the woods, from the camp. Hah. Gave that soldier a good drubbing, now none of them are hounding us.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Oof... We're safe here. I'll treat my injuries first, then I'll head back and tell everyone to come this way and meet up with you.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: People with Fionn's naff skills shouldn't be sticking around so long on the battlefield. Ought to be fighters like me.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Tch. You're miles better at fighting than he is, too.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: ...Selmon, there's a huge din behind us. What happened?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: All I can see is... a faint glow.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Hah, rotten shame you don't get to see proper. It's the fire from Reed's Arts, no doubt about it.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Is it a fine sight?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: But, well, I've known all along she was capable of that.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: ...Was night always this cold, out in the wilds...?

a.text: Suppose you're willing to light your fire. Will that make it a little warmer... a little brighter?
I don't know why you're disappointed in Dublinn, or why they're disappointed in you. The Tarans want to survive. They should survive. It's the simplest logic. How can any of it be a lie?
Before you leave the group, I need to talk to you about the whole—'going to Dublinn' thing. You'd know the way, right?
Moran, we'll head forward a little more. It'll be safer that way. Don't be afraid. It's all muddy here. If those soldiers retreat, they won't be coming this way.
Besides, the sun should be almost up.

steps.text: Their step finally slows. Moran no longer staggers trying to keep up.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Selmon, are we somewhere safe now?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I'm not afraid of bad news... Tell me.
They walk forward. Amongst the howl of the wind, distant explosions, and the cries, Moran tries her hardest to discern the sound of Selmon.
There should've been some forewarning, in that moment. Selmon should've stopped in her tracks, said something. At the very least, a scornful cackle at the fate of the Tarans.
But what Moran feels is simple; a step made, and the hand in hers falls, all of a sudden.
And she stoops, and cannot tell if what she feels is thick blood or wet mud.
